scope: Static source audit of identities, existing contact records, local assembly lifecycles, closure order, and reader grouping. No new collision/backend/render or physical check.

findings.classification: source-confirmed ordering conflict; physical concern reported
findings.observation: Both parallel beams are tied and joined before either double-ended pin is introduced. Each pin has source catalog contacts to both beams; the pin collar is centred at their common face.
findings.impact: A late pin instruction can require reopening the already tied chassis. Redrawing the same order does not repair this.
findings.cheapest_next_proof: Dry-fit one beam with both pins, then mate the second beam before ties. Verify collar seating and force before accepting the revised order.
findings.disposition: Candidate reorders and updates core membership; unaccepted.

findings.classification: source-confirmed ordering/grouping conflict; physical concern reported
findings.observation: Front dish191 precedes lower tie190; brackets183/184 and cap182 share raw33. Reader13 merges33–35 with zero detail frames. Source elevations form lower tie / bracket foot / upper cap layers.
findings.impact: The front dish can obstruct access; the combined panel also conceals the bracket/cap order.
findings.cheapest_next_proof: Dry-fit lower tie then brackets then cap, slopes and trim without191; add191 from the underside last. Check the final dish still seats without disassembly.
findings.disposition: Candidate builds a nine-piece front lower bumper locally on the table, joins via cap182 to168/177, then adds191. New join clearance unverified; unaccepted.

findings.observation: All four recipes pair inner arm/pivot, outer pin/carrier, then wheel pin/ball pin; complete units join later. Source confirmed contacts establish intended mates but not pin insertion or finger access.
findings.impact: A same-panel pair can hide which side receives a pin first; joining a finished unit to the corrected chassis still needs approach evidence.
findings.cheapest_next_proof: Check one left and one right inner-arm/pivot and outer pin/carrier pair with actual parts, then all four joins. Preserve each asymmetric pose and do not infer symmetry certification.
findings.disposition: No reorder: retain source until pair and unit approach checks identify an actual blocker.

findings.observation: Floor plates99/129 arrive at36 after suspension/bands but before both carriers. Narrow supports63/111/91/151 arrive at42. These become the fixed prefix for side-carrier joins.
findings.impact: Once both floor plates and support layers are installed, later brackets may need approach space that final contacts do not describe.
findings.cheapest_next_proof: Use the exact step18/19 prefix to inspect underside-facing carrier brackets against floor edges; compare deferring only the obstructing closure if a real obstruction is established.
findings.disposition: Do not defer floors speculatively: they support subsequent layers and may create unsupported prefixes.

findings.classification: captain-confirmed local access issue; mirrored source pattern
findings.observation: Two upper brackets precede top rails, then three remaining upper brackets attach to those rails. Right:82/87→333/81→93/89/83. Left:39/46→38/331→42/41/48. The last brackets are added after rail closure, but the local unit has no floor underneath yet.
findings.impact: Captain identifies the three right-angle parts under plates already attached to two brackets as the reported issue. Moving the last three earlier alone can restore floating pieces; each rail must first carry its own brackets as a separate local unit.
findings.cheapest_next_proof: Dry-fit each newly authored complete rail/bracket unit before joining the lower carrier, separately from whole-carrier installation; verify seating without force and distinguish awkward gripping from necessary removal.
findings.disposition: Candidate builds two separate upper rail units per side with all brackets fitted before each rail joins the lower carrier. Four shared running-board frames remain unchanged. Physical seating remains unverified.

findings.classification: suspected obstruction; retained unresolved near-seat witnesses
findings.observation: The full15-piece right carrier joins at58 after floor99/129 and supports111/151. Retained above-path evidence names156/99 and166/129 as unreported near-seat pairs;83/111 and93/151 are reported stud pairs. Left has96/99,115/129 and42/63,48/91. This differs from local recipe assembly.
findings.impact: Simultaneous upper seating and lower bracket/floor-edge clearance is unresolved. Finished-pose images and connected-prefix checks cannot prove a top-down route.
findings.cheapest_next_proof: First dry-fit right carrier into exact installed prefix, observing156/99 and166/129 from underneath. Record whether separation or only finger access is needed; then test left. If blocked, compare deferred floor closure vs split carrier installation with fresh lifecycle checks.
findings.disposition: No geometry change or fabricated motion. Existing top labels remain inherited unverified intent; do not treat them as certified.

findings.classification: previously corrected dependency retained; near-seat limits remain
findings.observation: Bed installation66 precedes rear trims206/214 at67. Prior evidence found100↔206 and118↔214 obstruction when those trims were already present. Near-seat bed/floor pairs100/99,109/99,118/99 remained unresolved.
findings.impact: Moving trims earlier would regress an existing correction. Current order does not establish every bed seating contact.
findings.cheapest_next_proof: Keep66 before67 as a regression assertion; dry-fit remaining near-seat bed/floor pairs only if acceptance needs them.
findings.disposition: No new defect claimed; candidate preserves corrected order.

findings.classification: suspected hidden layering and ergonomic access
findings.observation: Rear strip/clip/corner courses and wheel-arch cap layers carry source contacts between consecutive raw operations but several reader groups show only the final combined state.
findings.impact: Reader can reverse dependent layers or lose access to clips/rope rings even though raw ordering is retained.
findings.cheapest_next_proof: Review the actual affected pages and dry-fit clip and rope-ring layers before caps; split panels only where an insertion dependency or practical ambiguity is demonstrated.
findings.disposition: Presentation/access suspects; do not bulk reorder merely because groups are long.

findings.classification: suspected mixed attachment axes and hidden layers
findings.observation: Front core→brackets→grille backing→slats precedes left/right curved bumper and light groups102/103. Hood supports104/105 later close the region. Raw102/103 themselves each introduce four parts.
findings.impact: One finished headlight/bumper panel can conceal inner-to-outer mating and hand access; combined source operations are not an insertion path.
findings.cheapest_next_proof: Check bracket/grille and each four-part lamp/curved bumper course before hood supports. Use exact part transforms to identify approach directions only after mate verification.
findings.disposition: No correction until local obstruction or ordering ambiguity is established.

findings.classification: ergonomic access with correct coarse closure order
findings.observation: Steering/dashboard/seat108–110 precede pillars/glazing111–114, windscreen115–116, hood117–118 and roof119. Several reader groups merge their raw layers; roof is explicitly removable.
findings.impact: Coarse order avoids seating the interior through an installed roof, but same-op steering pair and glazing/cap access are not certified.
findings.cheapest_next_proof: Inspect steering pair199/200 and glazing/frame cap seating before roof; retain interior-before-roof constraints and use visible ordered panels if the page hides the mate.
findings.disposition: No confirmed new trapped part; no auto-reorder.

findings.classification: compound approach retained; physical seating and presentation pending
findings.observation: Mounts145 precede helm and panels; all three panel units install before outboard rails164 and tall masts175 onward. Accepted shield evidence is a bounded compound-path record, not a generic top insertion.
findings.impact: Collapsing it to one straight top arrow or adding rails/flags early can invalidate intended access.
findings.cheapest_next_proof: Review exact compound approach and stud-section evidence for current unchanged panel poses, then physically seat mounts/panels before rails and flags.
findings.disposition: Candidate preserves this order and does not fabricate vectors or claim new sweep coverage.

findings.observation: Speakers are capped after cones; sail clips follow wedge tie; banner collar precedes mast and flags; figures are supplied and placed last. These preserve plausible coarse access order, but connector fit and small-part gripping are untested.
findings.impact: Repeated recipes can hide per-copy access; final figure placement is not evidence of physical stability.
findings.cheapest_next_proof: Dry-fit cone sockets and flag clips locally, then install under the actual prefix. Preserve supplied-figure semantics and exact copy identity.
findings.disposition: No new confirmed ordering correction; maintain existing physical limits.
